findings.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/partition_prune.go:50` `handleDroppingForRange` can return an empty partition list for `DROP PARTITION` WriteOnly when `partitionNames` is set and the overlapping partition name is not included (`pkg/planner/core/partition_prune.go:77`). `pkg/planner/core/fragment.go:494` (TiFlash MPP dynamic prune path) turns an empty result into reading a real partition anyway, including the explicitly requested `partitionNames[0]` (`pkg/planner/core/fragment.go:517`). This path is exercised when `UseDynamicPartitionPrune()` is true and TiFlash MPP tasks are built (`pkg/planner/core/fragment.go:554`, call at `pkg/planner/core/fragment.go:561`), and the MPP request is built from the chosen physical partition IDs/ranges (`pkg/planner/core/fragment.go:632`).
findings.fix: In TiFlash MPP dynamic pruning, do not turn “no partitions” into “read some real partition”. Options: (1) build an MPP request that is non-empty but guaranteed to return 0 rows (e.g., one partition entry with a guaranteed-empty key range / out-of-table range), or (2) when pruning yields 0 partitions, force a non-MPP fallback (TiKV) / TableDual for this scan so `PARTITION(p_drop)` stays empty.
findings.impact: Queries that explicitly select a dropping partition (e.g., `SELECT * FROM t PARTITION(p0)`) during `DROP PARTITION` state changes can return rows from the logically dropped partition when executed via TiFlash MPP with dynamic partition pruning, violating DROP PARTITION visibility semantics and producing inconsistent results vs. TiKV/static pruning.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): the same “empty -> pick a partition to read” fallback still exists (moved to `pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/fragment.go`).
findings.verify: Repro on a TiFlash-enabled cluster with `tidb_partition_prune_mode=dynamic` and MPP enabled/enforced: while `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION p0` is in progress and some node/session is at the write-only schema version, run `SELECT * FROM t PARTITION(p0)` with `tidb_isolation_read_engines='tiflash'`. Expected: empty (dropped partition is non-readable). Actual (with current fallback): may scan `p0` and return its physical rows.
findings.what: TiFlash MPP dynamic partition pruning incorrectly overrides an empty pruned-partition set by selecting a real partition to scan (including the explicitly requested partition name), which can expose rows from partitions that are supposed to be non-readable during `DROP PARTITION` state changes.

subject: *: Drop partition DDL handling for overlapping partitions during State Changes (#56082)
summary: Implements overlapping-partition handling for `DROP PARTITION` state changes via new `PartitionInfo` helpers (`DDLAction`/`DDLState`, default list partition detection, overlapping index mapping), updates table partition location to error on writes/reads into dropping partitions, and updates planner static/dynamic pruning + point-get pruning to redirect reads to overlapping partitions and skip dropping partitions (with new multi-domain DDL tests).
